stem: A client has sharp pleuritic chest pain that worsens when lying flat and improves when leaning forward, and a pericardial friction rub is heard. Which condition is most likely?
rationale: Current NCBI/StatPearls describes acute pericarditis as classically causing severe pleuritic, positional chest pain that improves with sitting up and leaning forward; a pericardial friction rub is a characteristic and highly specific examination finding. Therefore B is the single best answer. The other conditions can cause chest discomfort but do not best explain this combined positional-pain and friction-rub pattern.
educational_objective: Recognize the characteristic chest-pain pattern and friction rub of acute pericarditis.
source_locator: History and Physical — classical pleuritic positional pain improves sitting/leaning forward; Physical Examination — pericardial friction rub characteristic/highly specific.
source_claim_supported: Pleuritic positional chest pain relieved by leaning forward plus a pericardial friction rub strongly supports acute pericarditis.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — acute/complex physiologic alterations and pathophysiology.

source_original.stem: A client has sharp pleuritic chest pain that worsens when lying flat and improves when leaning forward, and a pericardial friction rub is heard. Which condition is most likely?
source_original.rationale: Sharp pleuritic positional chest pain that improves when sitting up or leaning forward, together with a pericardial friction rub, is characteristic of acute pericarditis, so Option B is correct. Myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, and gastroesophageal reflux can cause chest discomfort but do not account for the characteristic pericardial friction rub plus this positional pain pattern.
source_original.source_detail: StatPearls Pericarditis — History and Physical: acute pericarditis classically causes severe pleuritic, positional chest pain that improves with sitting up and leaning forward; examination may reveal a pericardial friction rub. Current StatPearls/NCBI Bookshelf Pericarditis entry, updated 2026-04-13; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, endocrine/vascular emergencies and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained original construct/key after verifying the April 2026 StatPearls update.

audit_findings.claim_audit: Uses characteristic findings without claiming they replace full diagnostic evaluation.

distractor_audit.A: Does not best fit positional pleuritic pain + rub
distractor_audit.C: May be pleuritic but does not explain pericardial rub

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: B uniquely explains the combined findings.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are common causes of chest discomfort.
